newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines eyes freeport in central Visayas.
newsitem.headline: Philippines eyes freeport in central Visayas.

text.p: A freeport zone is being eyed in Leganes town in Iloilo, the Coordinating Council of the Philippine Assistance Programme (CCPAP) said on Monday.
CCPAP is a government agency tasked to oversee all foreign funded projects in the country.

CCPAP chairman Roberto de Ocampo and Leganes mayor Josil Jaen have signed a memorandum of agreement to study the viability of the plan through a grant from the U.S. Agency for International Development.
"(Leganes) is envisioned to become a rationally planned industrial centre, with an export processing zone to be developed as a freeport for the entire Visayas," CCPAP said in a statement.
Leganes will also serve as the extension of the Pavia Regional Agri-Industrial Centre, an existing special economic zone.

"The Leganes industrial growth centre will be an ideal industrial haven for industries locating in the Visayas. It will channel development to the Visayan countryside and provide more economic opportunities to the people," De Ocampo said.
The USAID masterplan will help the government draw up operation plans and on-site and off-site development projects for the Leganes freeport zone.
